channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
item.description: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

item.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
item.description: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

item.title: FAA ground stop live updates: FAA chief says when he expects air travel to recover
item.description: The administrator said the ground stop was the result of equipment failure.

item.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
item.description: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

item.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
item.description: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.

item.title: French Cyril Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit
item.description: Ciryl Gane remains the world's MMA heavyweight champion. Overnight, the French athlete beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in ​New York. The 5-round fight was rough, as Shirli Sitbon explains.

item.title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
item.description: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

item.title: France's presidential race heats up
item.description: In approximately six months time, French voters will head to the polls for the first round of the presidential election. Due to term limits, current president Emmanuel Macron is barred from running again. But that hasn't stopped a whole host of candidates from tossing their hat in the ring.

item.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's petrochemical capital in overnight assault
item.description: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that the central industrial city of Nizhnekamsk had endured "prolonged" Ukrainian airstrikes overnight, damaging a residential building and sparking a fire at a major petrochemical complex, injuring three people. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.

item.title: Pope crosses Peru in finale of trip home to visit flock high in Andes, deep in Amazon
item.description: The plight of Indigenous peoples and the protection of the Amazon take center stage on Pope Leo XIV’s penultimate day in Peru as he visits communities in the Andes and the rainforest

item.title: The Philippines and Australia strengthen joint military deterrence at ASEAN summit
item.description: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. During three days, world leaders are expected to focus on trade, energy and conflict – including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is expected to land in Manila on Tuesday. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.

item.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
item.description: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian president also claims that Russia has rejected an energy truce. This week’s US-mediated negotiations did not result in any tangible progress. Story by Simon Moritz.

item.title: UPS plane, Copa Airlines flight collide on taxiway at Miami International Airport
item.description: Two people were treated on the scene for minor injuries, airport officials said.

item.title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
item.description: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.

item.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia, overshadowed by tensions in Africa
item.description: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov.

item.title: Man dies after being struck by ambulance
item.description: A man has died after being hit by an ambulance that was taking a patient to hospital near Sunderland, police said.

item.title: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
item.description: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.

item.title: Are we too reliant on technology? Questions arise after Microsoft's widespread outages
item.description: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.

item.title: Minister says 'fundamental reset' of system needed as NEETs review looms
item.description: A minister has told Sky News a "fundamental reset" of the system was needed to help 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, work or training (NEET).

item.title: Pope laments poverty-stricken Inca communities as locals leave Peru
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.

item.title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
item.description: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.

item.title: Philippine star Carmelle wins first Asian edition of Eurovision song contest
item.description: The Philippines has won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest. The Filipino singer beat ten other acts to take the title in Bangkok, with a song celebrating women's empowerment. A taste of the winning song with Jack Pownall.

item.title: Two planes collide while taxiing at Miami airport - as two suffer minor injuries
item.description: Two planes have collided while taxiing at Miami airport, with the wingtip of a passenger jet striking the nose of a cargo aircraft, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has said.

item.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
item.description: In several states, Democrats took control of legislatures that had been divided and they weakened GOP dominance in others. Issues on the agenda: More access to health care, new limits on school vouchers. (Image credit: Sarah Kallis)

item.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
item.description: Being Heumann , premiering November 13, 2026 on Apple TV.'/> The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today. (Image credit: Apple TV)

item.title: New Mexico wanted free childcare for all. This is what's worked — and what hasn't
item.description: A year ago in November, New Mexico became the first state to offer free childcare to every eligible family, regardless of income. (Image credit: Nina Alexandria Riggio for NPR)

item.title: Iran claims attack on US military airbase in Bahrain
item.description: Iranian military confirmed on Sunday an attack on a US military base in Bahrain, in its second targeting the Middle Eastern country in the space of three days. Bahrain's military said it had intercepted several Iranian attacks, with the foreign ministry confirming its air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones, preventing them from reaching their intended targets.

item.title: SpaceX makes rocketry history by recapturing massive reusable rocketship
item.description: After failing to catch a booster yesterday, SpaceX managed to recapture its massive reusable rocketship, "Starship" for the first time. Smaller previous models have successfully relanded but they require heavy legs and aren't fully reusable. Story by Daniel Quinlan.

item.title: Zinédine Zidane returns to Bordeaux as France take on Turkey in Nations League
item.description: France will need to avoid defeat against Turkey, who they face in Bordeaux on Sunday night, to seal their spot in this season's Nations League quarter-finals. The match will see head coach Zinédine Zidane return to the city in which he spent four seasons as a player.

item.title: WATCH: Skylar's big surprise by the New England Patriots
item.description: Sixteen-year-old Skylar, a pediatric cancer patient, got an extra surprise from New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye while spending a day baking with Ann Michael Maye.

item.title: Savings app Chip targets retail investors in private market first
item.description: A British tech company is offering retail investors the chance to buy its shares in a first for the new private securities market that the London Stock Exchange (LSE) hopes will encourage more fast-growing scale-ups to remain in the UK.

item.title: Three sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
item.description: A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced the three gunmen responsible for a terror attack on a church funeral procession in the village of Hamoud that killed nine and wounded others. The attack prompted retaliatory strikes on "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria.

item.title: Cape Verde could make election history with first female president
item.description: Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.

item.title: 'Is this a cyberattack?' Grounded flights, a Microsoft outage and AI chaos fuel cybersecurity fears
item.description: A series of unsettling disruptions, from tech stock turbulence and Microsoft outages to a nationwide grounding of flights, has left millions wondering whether the world’s increasingly interconnected technology systems are beginning to unravel.

item.title: Hamas says senior commander killed in Israeli airstrike
item.description: A senior Hamas commander who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack had been killed in an Israeli airstrike, according to the Palestinian militant group.

item.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on Washington public golf course redevelopment
item.description: A federal judge on Saturday ordered a two-week delay to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House. (Image credit: Tom Brenner)

item.title: More cold health alerts to take effect after temperatures drop to -6C
item.description: Frosty conditions are expected to persist into next week, as more cold health alerts have been issued for parts of the UK on Sunday night until Thursday morning.

item.title: FAA ground stop disrupts college football
item.description: Some college football games were delayed a few hours on Saturday or postponed to Sunday. And in Oklahoma at least, there will be perks for fans to make up for the inconvenience, including cheap beers. (Image credit: Justin Ford)

item.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
item.description: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run. (Image credit: Alex Wong)

item.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
item.description: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization. (Image credit: Amy Maxmen)

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
item.description: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it. (Image credit: Eric Gay)

item.title: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever mid-air catch after return from orbit
item.description: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft made a successful return to Earth on Saturday, completing its first mid-air catch by giant robot arms in Texas, after an aborted recovery attempt.

item.title: New Orleans port officials sue owner of tanker that hit river cruise boat
item.description: The American Heritage river cruise paddleboat is seen on its side after being struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker ship in the Mississippi River, Friday. Pic: AP Photo/Gerald Herbert

item.title: WATCH: Elementary school named after beloved custodian
item.description: Marilyn Hampton was a beloved custodian for the Aubrey Independent School District outside Dallas, Texas. She was surprised with a school named in her honor, Marilyn Hampton Elementary School.

item.title: Wales beat the All Blacks for first time since 1953
item.description: Wales have beaten New Zealand in a men's rugby union match for the first time in 73 years.

item.title: Microsoft confirms all services are restored after global outage
item.description: Microsoft has said that all services have been fully restored after a global outage which affected the NHS, police, schools and other services across the UK.

item.title: US asked if Ukraine would give up parts of Donbas for NATO membership, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The US has asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region if Kyiv were admitted to NATO, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold unprecedented meeting, White House says
item.description: The leaders of the US, China and Russia will hold an unprecedented meeting on the sidelines of a major economic summit, the White House has said.

item.title: Goalkeeper given 12-game ban for fatal collision with Tenerife striker
item.description: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 games after an on-field collision that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Lauren Boebert will lose her seat in Congress to Democrat Laubacher, AP projects
item.description: Colorado Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert will lose her House seat to Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, The Associated Press projected Friday.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders receives 2028 presidential encouragement
item.description: Supporters and donors have been encouraging GOP Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders to run for president in the 2028 cycle, sources told ABC News.

item.title: Congressional Republicans push Howard Lutnick, Jensen Huang to testify about Nvidia
item.description: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, a Republican, sent letters to both Huang and Lutnick to publicly testify in front of the committee

item.title: Schumer and Van Hollen face off for Senate majority leader. What do Democrats think?
item.description: Within moments of Chris Van Hollen announcing his intent to challenge Chuck Schumer in a race to lead next year’s Senate Democratic majority, endorsements began flying.

item.title: EU leaders choose team for Ukraine peace talks after months of wavering
item.description: British representatives will be part of a team representing Europe in Ukraine peace talks.

item.title: WATCH: 41-year-old firefighter’s life saved by heart transplant
item.description: Nico Ratto, a dad of two from New Jersey, spent 45 days hospitalized before receiving a lifesaving heart transplant.

item.title: WATCH: Heartwarming update on Punch the Monkey
item.description: The baby macaque at Japan’s Ichikawa City Zoo became a viral sensation after turning to an IKEA toy for comfort. Nine months later, Punch has joined the troop and taken an interest in a baby macaque.

item.title: WATCH: Empire State Building climbers appear in court
item.description: The daredevil couple who were arrested after climbing to the top of the Empire State Building were in court on Thursday to face criminal charges and possible deportation.

item.title: Republicans dazed by midterm election defeats grapple with what went wrong
item.description: Republicans are grappling with unexpected losses after the midterm elections

item.title: Maryland Sen. Van Hollen says he will challenge Sen. Schumer for Democratic leader
item.description: Maryland Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge New York Sen. Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader in the new Congress.

item.title: WATCH: School's ultimate class trip heads to Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New reports on a group of middle schoolers in Maryland who are about to get the snow day of their lives in the form of a class trip to Antarctica.

item.title: WATCH: Tanker truck driver narrowly avoids train crash in Fort Worth
item.description: A tanker truck driver managed to escape from his vehicle just seconds before a train slammed into his truck.

item.title: US soldier accused of spying for Russia identified: Source
item.description: US officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

item.title: Colom’s historic Senate win could reshape Mississippi’s political future: Analysis
item.description: The question is whether his victory can establish a lasting realignment.

item.title: Republicans push for Jensen Huang's testimony following Nvidia CEO's resignation
item.description: "I don't think he's got anything to hide now. Let it fly," Rep. Burchett said.

item.title: WATCH: United Airlines banning AI bots from booking flights
item.description: The airline says customers who give their personal and credit card information to AI businesses run the risk of having their sensitive data exposed.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, health ministry says
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on a Palestinian hospital has killed at least six and wounded 28, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.
